note: Known answers per script family. These pin the analyser: a change to any of them is a change to every text index built with it, so a diff here must be accompanied by a bump to ANALYSER_VERSION and a rebuild. They were produced by the shipped Analyser and read back by a human against the design's rules, not copied from a second library.

vectors.why: Diacritics are NOT folded — o with umlaut stays distinct from o, because they are different letters in Swedish and the same in German, and a wrong default corrupts recall silently. The sharp s does fold, because full case folding maps it to ss.

vectors.why: KNOWN GAP, stated not hidden: icu_segmenter 2.2 carries no Khmer model, so the run is not word-segmented and is indexed as one token. That matches a whole-field query and not a word within it. records-and-search.md 4.4 names Khmer among the six scripts needing dictionary segmentation; lindera is the design's named escalation.
One analyser, nothing declared, and no run lost at a script boundary. Both CJK runs here are the single-word shape that the word-like flag drops.

vectors.why: An arXiv id survives as one token because the dots sit between digits and letters; the colon and brackets do not. A keyword column is still the right home for exactness — this only says what text does with one.
NFKC maps fullwidth forms to their ASCII compatibility equivalents, so a fullwidth query finds a halfwidth document.
UAX 29 keeps the apostrophe inside a contraction and breaks on the hyphen. Stated because it is the pair a reader most often expects to behave alike.
